title: OPM.executeOperation never checks initiator: any caller can start a flashloan with onBehalfOf = a credit-delegating victim and params.user = attacker
description: Discovery: MODIFIER-01 / AC-03 (flashloan receiver authorization). The only caller check is lendingPool == msg.sender (inside executeBuyOptions/executeLiquidation), and the lending pool is selected by the attacker-controlled poolId in params. `initiator` is unused, and `user`, `sourceSwap`, `collateral` are decoded from params. buyOptions is the only legitimate producer of mode 0 params and sets onBehalfOf = msg.sender = user. Since anyone can call lendingPool.flashLoan(receiver = OPM, modes = [2], onBehalfOf = X, params), the pair (onBehalfOf, params.user) is not bound together. Confirms and deepens DP1-1. Also applicable to mode 1 (any non-zero mode): a mode-2 flashloan with liquidation params opens debt on the victim while the TR tokens re-minted by closeDebt remain in the OPM.
root_cause: The receiver trusts calldata params for the beneficiary of the flashloan proceeds instead of binding it to the initiator or to the debt holder (onBehalfOf). Credit delegation granted to the OPM by a buyOptions user is therefore usable by any third party.

harm.who: any user who has approved credit delegation of a TR debt token to the OPM
harm.loses_what: variable TR debt opened in their name while the underlying proceeds are deposited as collateral for the attacker
harm.magnitude: up to the victim's delegated borrow allowance

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls approveDelegation(OPM, large) on the TR variable debt token to use buyOptions.
2. Attacker calls lendingPool.flashLoan(OPM, [TR], [amt], [2], victim, abi.encode(uint8(0), poolId, attacker, [address(0)]), 0) directly.
3. Pool opens variable debt for the victim and calls OPM.executeOperation; msg.sender == lendingPool passes, initiator is ignored.
4. withdrawOptionAssets burns the TR into token0/token1 and cleanup(lendingPool, attacker, token) deposits them to the attacker's account (repaying the attacker's own debt first if any).
5. Attacker withdraws the collateral; the victim holds unbacked TR debt and can be liquidated.

preconditions.text: victim has delegated borrowing of a TR debt token to the OPM
attacker can call lendingPool.flashLoan directly

postconditions.text: victim holds TR variable debt with no matching collateral

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓ (killed by FP-1)
audit_trail.missing_precondition: victim delegation to the attacker (not to OPM)
postconditions_created: victim holds TR variable debt with no matching collateral

verdict.reason: Authorization is enforced in the lending pool: an Aave-v2-style flashLoan with modes!=0 mints debt via DebtToken.mint(msg.sender, onBehalfOf) which spends the borrow allowance of onBehalfOf granted to msg.sender of flashLoan. A direct attacker call needs the victim's delegation to the attacker, not to the OPM; only OPM.buyOptions (msg.sender = OPM, onBehalfOf = msg.sender) can use the delegation granted to the OPM. Trace step 3 fails. Pool is out of scope; relies on standard Aave v2 behaviour.

title: OPM.close is callable by anyone for any user: PMTransfers the victim's whole token0/token1 balances, charges a 1% fee on their collateral and swaps with maxAmount = the victim's entire balance
description: Discovery: MODIFIER-01 sibling diff. sellOptions, withdrawOptions and swapTokens all PMTransfer from msg.sender, but close() takes an arbitrary `user` with no msg.sender == user check, no health or liquidatability check. The OPM is a PMTransfer-whitelisted contract, so this single param decides whose aTokens are pulled. closeDebt withdraws ALL of the user's token0 and token1 aTokens, charges a 1% treasury fee out of the user's collateral when user != msg.sender, and if one side is short calls swapTokensForExactTokens(router, shortfall, maxAmount = other-side whole balance). The only guard is getAmountsIn from the same AMM, so there is no price protection (checkExpectedBalances only checks the TR deposit amounts, not the swap). Confirms and deepens DP1-2.
root_cause: A permissionless entry point operates on a third party's assets via PMTransfer without any authorization and with a swap whose limit is derived from the same pool it trades against.

harm.who: any user with an open TR debt in a ROE pool served by the OPM
harm.loses_what: collateral lost to forced swaps at attacker-set prices plus a 1% fee on the closed debt, on a position they did not choose to close
harm.magnitude: up to the victim's whole balance of the swapped-in token per call

exploit_trace: 1. Victim has TR debt and holds token0 collateral only; closing requires token1 so a swap is needed.
2. Attacker front-runs by moving the Uniswap V3 pool price against the required swap direction.

3. Attacker calls close(poolId, victim, debtAsset, 0, collateral): OPM pulls all victim aTokens, getAmountsIn quotes the manipulated pool, amountsIn <= maxAmount (victim's entire balance) passes, swap executes at the bad price.
4. Attacker back-runs to restore the price and keeps the profit; the victim's debt is repaid but collateral is reduced by the price impact plus the 1% fee.

preconditions.text: victim has TR debt registered in the pool
victim's collateral mix needs a swap to repay the TR

postconditions.text: victim position closed and collateral reduced, possibly below health

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R10:✓(worst case = whole balance as maxAmount)
postconditions_created: victim position closed and collateral reduced

verdict.reason: close() has no msg.sender==user or health check; PMWithdraw pulls all of the victim's token0/token1 aTokens, 1% fee charged on third-party close, exact-output swap bounded only by the victim's whole balance (OptionsPositionManager.sol:223-241, 275-304, 491-504). Comment at line 280 suggests third-party soft liquidation is intended, so severity rests on the missing health check and the sandwichable swap. PoC recommended.

title: GeVault withdraw burns shares for 0 once funds are parked idle: with isEnabled=false every withdrawal after the first pays nothing
description: Discovery: Q2 (accountant, trace every wei) / TVL-01. withdraw() prices shares from getTVL(), which only sums aToken balances of the ticks (getTickBalance). withdraw() and rebalance() both call removeFromAllTicks() and only redeploy `if (isEnabled)`. When the owner has set isEnabled=false (the documented way to wind the pool down: 'otherwise just let assets sit here until totally withdrawn'), the first withdraw or any public rebalance() moves every position into idle token0/token1 balances of the vault. From then on getTVL()==0, so valueX8 and amount are 0 for every later withdrawer, yet _burn(msg.sender, liquidity) still executes and no check requires amount>0. The idle tokens stay in the vault and are not attributable to any share.
root_cause: Share valuation (getTVL) ignores the vault's own idle token0/token1 balances, while the disabled path deliberately parks all assets idle; withdraw has no amount>0 check.

harm.who: every vault depositor who withdraws after the first withdrawal/rebalance while the pool is disabled
harm.loses_what: their whole share value (shares burned, 0 paid)
harm.magnitude: up to the entire vault TVL minus the first withdrawer's share

exploit_trace: 1. Owner calls setEnabled(false) to wind the vault down; ticks still hold all assets as aTokens.
2. User A calls withdraw(): TVL is still correct, A is paid, removeFromAllTicks() moves every other depositor's assets to idle balances and deployAssets() is skipped.
3. User B calls withdraw(all): getTVL() sums only aToken balances and returns 0, so amount = 0; the fee transfer and payout transfer move 0, _burn destroys B's shares.
4. Alternatively anyone calls rebalance() right after setEnabled(false) to park everything idle, making every following withdrawal pay 0.

preconditions.text: owner sets isEnabled=false while depositors remain

postconditions.text: vault holds idle tokens unaccounted by any share; later withdrawers lose all value

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
postconditions_created: idle vault balances outside TVL
audit_trail.who_benefits: Nobody directly; funds remain stuck for the owner (or are captured by the next depositor after re-enable)

verdict.reason: Confirmed GeVault.sol:214-241 and 392-398: getTVL sums only TR aToken balances, withdraw/rebalance leave assets idle when isEnabled is false, later withdraw computes amount 0 and still burns shares. Requires the owner to disable the pool (documented wind-down) with depositors remaining. PoC recommended.

title: V3Proxy: swapTokensForExactETH keeps the unspent amountInMax and swapTokensForExactTokens refunds the entire proxy balance, so stranded input is claimable by the next caller
description: Discovery: Q4.4 (amountIn < amountInMax boundary) and Module F. Both exact-output paths pull amountInMax from the caller, but the router only consumes amountIn <= amountInMax. swapTokensForExactETH never returns amountInMax-amountIn, so it stays in the proxy. swapTokensForExactTokens refunds ogInAsset.balanceOf(address(this)), which includes any previously stranded balance of that token, so the next caller of the exact-token path with the same path[0] (amountInMax can be small) receives the leftovers. The function is also payable but ETH sent is not used. Deepens DP1-4.
root_cause: Refund logic is not tied to this call's delta (amountInMax - amountIn); one path omits the refund, the other refunds the full balance.
vulnerable_code:
amounts[0] = ROUTER.exactOutputSingle(...amountInMax...);
...
ogInAsset.safeApprove(address(ROUTER), 0);   // swapTokensForExactETH: no refund
...
ogInAsset.safeTransfer(msg.sender, ogInAsset.balanceOf(address(this)));   // swapTokensForExactTokens

harm.who: callers of swapTokensForExactETH (and contracts integrating it)
harm.loses_what: amountInMax - amountIn of the input token on every call
harm.magnitude: the slippage margin per call, taken by the next swapTokensForExactTokens caller or the owner via emergencyWithdraw

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls swapTokensForExactETH(amountOut, amountInMax = 1.01*quote, [USDC, WETH]); router spends the quote, 1% of USDC stays in V3Proxy.
2. Attacker calls swapTokensForExactTokens(1 wei, 1, [USDC, X]) (any valid direct path with USDC as input).
3. The final safeTransfer sends ogInAsset.balanceOf(proxy), including the victim's stranded USDC, to the attacker.

preconditions.text: a swapTokensForExactETH call with amountInMax above the real input

postconditions.text: stranded token balance sits in the proxy

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R11:✓(unsolicited balance claimed by balanceOf refund)
postconditions_created: stranded token balance sits in the proxy

verdict.reason: V3Proxy.sol:160-176 swapTokensForExactETH never refunds amountInMax-amountIn; swapTokensForExactTokens (line 132) refunds the whole proxy balance of path[0], so stranded input is claimable by any later caller. Real but bounded by the slippage margin callers supply; no in-scope contract uses the ETH path. Downgraded from High.

title: Permissionless helpers sweep the contract's whole token balance to the caller: PositionManager.cleanup via liquidate/OPM entry points and RangeManager.cleanup via removeAssetsFromStep
description: Discovery: Module O / state lifecycle (balanceOf(this)-based payout). RangeManager.cleanup deposits balanceOf(address(this)) of both assets to msg.sender, and removeAssetsFromStep(step) is permissionless: any caller (even with no position, step valid) receives everything the contract holds. initRange (owner) pushes amounts into TR.init, which refunds unused tokens to the RangeManager (msg.sender of init), and initRange only forwards the TR tokens back, so the refund (up to 5% slippage margin) is left in RangeManager and is claimable by the first caller. Same pattern in OPM: PositionManager.cleanup(LP, user, asset) pays balanceOf(this) to `user`, and liquidate() calls it with msg.sender, so any stray OPM balance (e.g. dust from closeDebt/liquidation, direct flashloans with mode 1) goes to the next liquidator. Confirms and deepens DP1-5.
root_cause: Payouts use the contract's entire balance instead of the amount derived from the caller's own operation.

harm.who: protocol owner (initRange refund) and users whose dust remains in the contracts
harm.loses_what: residual token0/token1 left in RangeManager/OPM
harm.magnitude: bounded by the Uniswap refund (up to ~5% of init amounts) and stray dust

exploit_trace: 1. Owner calls initRange(tr, amount0, amount1); TR.init mints at the pool ratio and refunds unused tokens to RangeManager; only TR tokens are forwarded to the owner.
2. Attacker calls removeAssetsFromStep(step) with a valid step and no position.
3. cleanup() deposits the leftover token0/token1 into the lending pool on behalf of the attacker, who then withdraws them (health factor passes when there is no debt).

preconditions.text: RangeManager or OPM holds a stray token balance

postconditions.text: stray balance transferred to the first caller

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✗ G=✓ H=✓
postconditions_created: stray balance moved to attacker account

verdict.reason: Stray balance sweep is real (RangeManager.cleanup/PositionManager.cleanup use balanceOf(this)) but the only stray funds are the TR.init refund (owner-chosen near-exact amounts, within the 5% min) and swap dust; max extractable is well under $100 (no native price recorded; assumed ordinary stablecoin/ETH amounts).

title: TokenisableRange.deposit splits the caller's tokens between fee pool and liquidity using slot0 spot, so a manipulated spot sends a two-sided depositor's tokens to the shared fee pool
description: Discovery: Q1/amm-mev-deep (spot read in value split), Module D/I. When fee0+fee1>0 and the caller supplies both sides, deposit() computes newFee0 = n0*fee0/(token0Amount+fee0) and newFee1 = n1*fee1/(token1Amount+fee1) where token0Amount/token1Amount come from IUniswapV3Pool.slot0() (flash-manipulable). If spot is pushed so the position holds almost no token0 (token0Amount -> 0), newFee0 -> n0 for any fee0>0 (even 1 wei): the caller's entire n0 is credited to fee0, the shared uncompounded fee pool, and only n1 (minus its fee share) is added as liquidity. LP minted is supply*newLiquidity/liquidity, so the depositor is not credited for the n0 moved to the fee pool, which is split among all LP holders. RangeManager.transferAssetsIntoStep (user collateral) and OPM.sellOptions call deposit without any oracle or spot guard; GeVault's guard (poolMatchesOracle) is not present there.
root_cause: Proportional fee/liquidity split is derived from spot slot0 instead of the oracle-derived price used elsewhere in the contract (returnExpectedBalanceWithoutFees), and there is no min-LP-out parameter.

harm.who: users depositing both tokens into a TR through RangeManager or OPM.sellOptions
harm.loses_what: most of one token side of the deposit, redistributed to existing LP holders (including the attacker)
harm.magnitude: up to the full n0 (or n1) minus the depositor's own pro-rata share; attacker gain = loss x attacker's LP share

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker holds a large share of a TokenisableRange that has any pending fee0>0 and fee1>0.
2. Victim submits transferAssetsIntoTickerStep/RangerStep(step, amount0, amount1) with both amounts non-zero.
3. Attacker front-runs by swapping the Uniswap V3 pool so spot sits at the range edge where token0Amount ~ 0 (cheap for a 10-tick ticker, flash-loan funded for a wide ranger).
4. deposit(): newFee0 ~ n0 so n0 is added to fee0; n0 ~ 0 goes to Uniswap; victim receives LP only for the n1-derived liquidity.
5. Attacker swaps back and withdraws; the victim's n0 sits in fee0 and is paid out pro rata to LP holders.

preconditions.text: TR has pending fee0 and fee1 (not yet compounded)
depositor supplies both tokens and caller has no spot guard
attacker can move slot0 of the TR's Uniswap pool within the block

postconditions.text: depositor's n0 credited to the shared fee pool

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
depth_evidence: [TRACE:slot0 spot -> token0Amount~0 -> newFee0=n0*fee0/(0+fee0)=n0 -> n0 set to 0 -> LP minted from n1 only]
postconditions_created: fee0 inflated by victim funds
audit_trail.who_benefits: Existing LP holders, notably an attacker holding most TR supply

verdict.reason: TokenisableRange.sol:237-247 uses slot0 for the fee/liquidity split; when spot is moved so the position holds none of token0, newFee0 = n0 and the depositor's token0 goes to the shared fee pool (no min-LP, amountMin is applied after the reduction). Requires pending fee0 and fee1 on the TR, a two-sided depositor via RangeManager/OPM.sellOptions and a flash-moveable pool; single-tick ranges make the move cheap. PoC recommended.

title: GeVault share price is manipulable by first-depositor donation: shares can be reduced to 1 wei and the vault donated to, so a following deposit mints rounded-down shares
description: Discovery: Q2/Edge Case first-depositor, vault-share-accounting module. deposit() mints liquidity = tSupply * valueX8 / vaultValueX8 with no minimum-liquidity burn and no virtual offset. TVL is read from aToken balances of the ticks, which can be inflated by a direct donation (send token0/token1 to the vault and call the public rebalance(), or deposit TR tokens in the lending pool on behalf of the vault). On a fresh vault the first depositor can withdraw all but 1 wei of shares (withdraw accepts any liquidity amount), leaving totalSupply=1 and TVL~0, then donate X value. A later deposit of V (X < V < 2X) mints floor(V/X)=1 share, i.e. half of the pool for a deposit of V, while the attacker holds the other share.
root_cause: Share minting rounds down against the depositor with a supply the first holder can reduce to 1 wei and a TVL that accepts donations; no dead shares or virtual assets.

harm.who: the next depositor(s) into a vault whose supply is held by a single attacker
harm.loses_what: up to roughly a sixth to a quarter of the deposit through share rounding
harm.magnitude: bounded by tvlCap (default 1e12 = 10,000 USD) unless the owner raises it

exploit_trace: 1. Vault is freshly deployed (totalSupply 0). Attacker deposits a small amount and gets shares.
2. Attacker calls withdraw(totalSupply-1, token): supply is now 1 wei, TVL ~ 0.
3. Attacker sends X of token0 to the vault and calls rebalance(), so getTVL() ~ X.
4. Victim deposits V with X < V < 2X (attacker front-runs the victim's pending deposit sized from the mempool): liquidity = 1 * V / X = 1.
5. Both hold 1 share of a pool worth X+V; victim loses about (V-X)/2-ish of value, attacker withdraws the gain.

preconditions.text: attacker is sole shareholder / vault supply can be reduced to a few wei
victim deposit is below 2x the donated TVL

postconditions.text: victim holds shares worth less than the deposit

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
postconditions_created: skewed share price

verdict.reason: Standard first-depositor/donation inflation: GeVault.sol:274-282 mints tSupply*valueX8/vaultValueX8 with no dead shares; attacker can reduce supply to 1 wei via withdraw and raise TVL by donation plus rebalance. Only applies while the attacker is the sole shareholder and victim deposit sits between X and 2X; loss bounded by tvlCap (default 1e12 = $10k).

title: OPM.closeDebt swaps with no price bound (maxAmount = user's whole balance, amountsIn quoted from the same manipulable pool): every close/liquidate swap leg is sandwichable
description: Discovery: Q4.5 / Module amm-mev-deep section 7 (zero slippage) and EXT-03. In closeDebt, when one underlying is short, swapTokensForExactTokens(router, shortfall, maxAmount, path) is called with maxAmount = the user's entire balance of the other token (amtA / amtB) or, in the liquidation path, the whole OPM balance. Inside, the only bound is amountsIn[0] <= maxAmount, and amountsIn comes from V3Proxy.getAmountsIn, i.e. the Uniswap V3 Quoter at the current (manipulable) pool price. checkExpectedBalances only validates the underlying amounts that will be deposited into the TR against the oracle (98-102 percent of the debt value); it does not bound what the swap costs. The swap leg therefore has no oracle-based limit, unlike swapExactTokensForTokens which applies oracle * 99 percent.
root_cause: The slippage guard of the exact-output swap is the caller's full balance, not an oracle-derived maximum input. The quote used to size the swap is read from the same pool the attacker can move in the same transaction.

harm.who: borrowers whose TR debt is closed (self-close or by a third party) and liquidators
harm.loses_what: part of the collateral swapped at a manipulated price
harm.magnitude: price distortion times swap size, bounded by the user's balance of the sold token

exploit_trace: 1. Victim holds a TR debt and collateral mostly in one underlying (say token1); the debt's TR needs token0.
2. Attacker front-runs by buying token0 in the V3 pool, pushing the price against the victim's swap direction.

3. close() (called by the victim or by the attacker as soft-liquidator) PMWithdraws all aTokens and calls swapTokensForExactTokens; Quoter prices the exact-output swap at the manipulated price and it passes because maxAmount is the victim's whole token1 balance.
4. Attacker back-runs, restores the price and keeps the difference; the victim receives the leftover after overpaying.

preconditions.text: position needs a swap to rebuild the TR underlying mix
UniV3 pool price movable by the attacker

postconditions.text: victim collateral reduced by the manipulation cost

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R10:✓(worst case = whole token balance as max input)
R16:✗(oracle not involved in swap bound)
depth_evidence: [TRACE:attacker swap -> close -> exact-output swap at distorted price -> back-run]
postconditions_created: swap executed at distorted price

verdict.reason: closeDebt (OptionsPositionManager.sol:293-304) bounds the exact-output swap only by the caller's whole balance with quote from the same pool; checkExpectedBalances covers only the TR deposit amounts. Overlaps DA-2's swap component; applies to self-close and liquidation legs.

title: GeVault deploys/rebalances at the Uniswap spot tick while the only manipulation guard is a 1 percent oracle band (ticks are about 0.1 percent wide): a permissionless rebalance sandwich makes the vault sell/buy at off-market tick prices
description: Discovery: Q4.5 and flash-loan-interaction section 0 (external flash susceptibility) / amm-mev-deep section 5-6. rebalance() is permissionless; it removes all liquidity and redeploys everything with getActiveTickIndex(), which classifies ticks using TokenisableRange.getTokenAmountsExcludingFees, i.e. the pool's slot0 spot. poolMatchesOracle only requires spot to be within 1 percent of the oracle ratio, while each ticker spans 10 Uniswap ticks (about 0.1 percent). An attacker can therefore move spot by up to about 0.9 percent in the same transaction, call rebalance() (or deposit/withdraw, which call it), so that the vault parks its token1 (or token0) in tickers positioned relative to the distorted price, then move the price back. The restoring trade runs through the vault's freshly placed liquidity, converting it at prices up to about 0.9 percent worse than the true price.
root_cause: Redeployment decisions use manipulable slot0 spot and the oracle band (1 percent) is an order of magnitude wider than the tick spacing; rebalance is callable by anyone at any time.

harm.who: GeVault share holders
harm.loses_what: a fraction of deployed assets as LVR to the attacker per sandwiched rebalance
harm.magnitude: up to roughly 0.9 percent of the assets redeployed, minus attacker swap fees

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker flash-borrows and swaps in the UniV3 pool to move spot up by about 0.9 percent (still inside the 1 percent band).
2. Attacker calls GeVault.rebalance(): all liquidity is withdrawn and token1 is redeployed into the tickers below the distorted price (some of which lie above the true price).
3. Attacker swaps back; the price falls through those tickers, converting the vault's token1 into token0 at prices above the true price.
4. Attacker repays the flash loan and keeps the spread.

preconditions.text: pool deep enough to be moved ~0.9 percent profitably relative to vault size

postconditions.text: vault assets converted at off-market prices

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✗ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R16:✓(oracle band wider than tick spacing)
depth_evidence: [VARIATION:spot +0.9 percent -> active tick index shifts ~9 ticks]
postconditions_created: vault positions parked at distorted ticks

verdict.reason: Speculative: ticks are discrete single-tick TRs far apart (test grid 100 USD on ~1262), so a <=0.9% spot move only changes active-tick selection near a boundary; attacker must pay pool fees both ways and vault size is capped by tvlCap (10,000 USD), so max take is under ~90 USD before costs. No concrete profitable trace with values (also Gate F).

title: GeVault deposit-in-one-token / withdraw-in-the-other settles at oracle prices with a ~0.2 percent fee, while the spot-vs-oracle guard allows 1 percent deviation: oracle-lag arbitrage against the vault
description: Discovery: Q4.5 / oracle-analysis (lag vs spot) / Q7.8. deposit(token, amount) mints shares at Chainlink-valued TVL after a fee of 0.1-0.3 percent (baseFeeX4 = 20, scaled 0.5x-1.5x), and withdraw(liquidity, token) lets the holder pick either pool token and pays valueX8 / oracle price of that token minus the same fee. A depositor can thus swap token A for token B through the vault at the Chainlink ratio. poolMatchesOracle lets the market (Uniswap spot) differ from the oracle by up to 1 percent, and Chainlink feeds update on a 0.5-1 percent deviation or heartbeat. Whenever the market ratio is more than the fee away from the oracle ratio, the round trip (deposit token A, withdraw token B in the same or a later block) is profitable and drains the vault's token B balance, repeatable until the oracle updates.
root_cause: Vault shares are priced at lagging oracle values and withdrawals in a chosen token are priced at the same oracle, with a fee smaller than the permitted oracle/market deviation.

harm.who: other GeVault share holders
harm.loses_what: value equal to the oracle/market gap minus fee on each round trip
harm.magnitude: up to ~0.5-0.8 percent of the amount cycled, bounded by tvlCap and vault token availability

exploit_trace: 1. Market moves 0.7 percent against the Chainlink ratio (inside the 1 percent band, before the feed updates).
2. Attacker deposits token A (fee ~0.2 percent) and receives shares valued at the stale oracle.
3. Attacker withdraws all shares in token B at the stale oracle ratio (fee ~0.2 percent).
4. Attacker sells token B on Uniswap at the market ratio and keeps ~0.3 percent; repeats until feed update or vault runs out of B.

preconditions.text: oracle/market gap larger than combined fees

postconditions.text: vault composition shifts toward the overvalued token

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✗ G=✓ H=✓
depth_evidence: [BOUNDARY:oracle gap=0.7 percent, fee round trip=0.4 percent]
audit_trail.missing_precondition: gap larger than fees at meaningful size
postconditions_created: vault holds more of the overvalued token

verdict.reason: Oracle-lag arbitrage: round-trip fee is about 0.2-0.6% (0.5x-1.5x of 0.2% each way), oracle gap that survives Chainlink deviation thresholds is about 0.5%, notional capped by tvlCap (10,000 USD) and by the vault balance of the withdrawn token; max profit per cycle is tens of dollars. Generic oracle-lag class; staleness is a known issue.

title: GeVault.deployAssets deposits a single token into the ticker that contains the spot price, so deposit/withdraw/rebalance revert whenever spot sits inside a listed ticker
description: Discovery: Q4.4 boundary (param=0 / one-sided input) on deployAssets. getActiveTickIndex breaks at the first i where tick i+1 holds no token0 and tick i+2 holds token0 (mirror for token1). Tick i+2 is therefore the first tick with the other token, which is the MIXED tick if the spot price lies inside a ticker range (amt0>0 and amt1>0). deployAssets then calls depositAndStash(ticks[tick0Index], availToken0/2, 0), i.e. TR.deposit(n0, 0) on an in-range tick. NPM.increaseLiquidity computes liquidity = min(L0, L1) = 0 for a one-sided in-range deposit and UniswapV3Pool.mint(0) reverts, so the whole call reverts. Tickers are 10 ticks wide and only revert when spot is inside one, but the oracle band in poolMatchesOracle is 1%, so spot can be pushed into a ticker while the guard still passes.
root_cause: Active-tick selection does not exclude the tick containing the current price, and deployAssets assumes the first tick holding the other token is wholly single-sided.

harm.who: GeVault depositors and withdrawers
harm.loses_what: ability to deposit, withdraw or rebalance (withdraw reverts after removeFromAllTicks only if isEnabled) while spot is inside a ticker

title: OptionsPositionManager.addDust is scaled in TR wei per underlying decimals, so closeDebt over-mints TR whose excess stays stuck in the OPM at the user's cost
description: Discovery: Q4.2 (mechanical arithmetic). addDust returns 10**(20-decimals)*price/1e8 interpreted as TR wei (1e18 = 1 TR) with the comment 'any underlying amount larger than 100 units'. That is only right if 1 TR is worth about $1. For a 6-decimal asset (USDC) it is 1e14 TR wei = 1e-4 TR regardless of TR value; a TR initialised with large liquidity is worth far more per unit, so the dust added to repayAmount and deposited is worth V*1e-4 per close/liquidation. LP.repay caps at the real debt, the excess TR remains in OPM (cleanup only handles token0/token1) and is only recoverable by removeDust to the treasury, so the user's (or liquidator's) funds pay for it.
root_cause: Dust is defined in underlying raw units but applied as TR wei without converting via the TR's value per unit.

harm.who: users whose debt is closed via OPM.close and liquidators
harm.loses_what: underlying tokens worth V_TR*1e-4 (USDC pair) per call, left as TR in the OPM
harm.magnitude: about $10 per call if 1 TR is worth $100k; negligible for small TRs

exploit_trace: 1. TR value per 1e18 units is V (e.g. $100k); pair has a 6-decimal token at $1.
2. Anyone calls close(poolId, user, TR, 0, collateral); debt = userDebt + 1e14.
3. closeDebt deposits getTokenAmounts(debt) underlying, minting about userDebt+1e14 TR; LP.repay consumes only userDebt.
4. 1e14 TR (worth V*1e-4) stays in OPM; user's aTokens paid for it.

preconditions.text: TR value per unit well above $1

postconditions.text: TR dust accumulates in the OPM

title: GeVault.deployAssets indexes ticks[newTickIndex+3] out of bounds when the price is beyond the listed ticks, bricking deposit/withdraw/rebalance
description: Discovery: Q5.6 / Q9 boundary check. getActiveTickIndex loops up to ticks.length - 3 and, if no boundary is found (price past the last listed ticks), returns ticks.length - 3. deployAssets then touches ticks[tick0Index + 1] with tick0Index = newTickIndex + 2, i.e. ticks[ticks.length], which reverts with out-of-bounds when both token balances are non-zero (or for the corresponding side). With ticks.length < 4 it always reverts. withdraw() calls deployAssets when enabled, so withdrawals also revert until the owner pushes more ticks.
root_cause: The active-index search does not leave room for the +3 offset used by deployAssets and has no guard for running out of ticks.

harm.who: all GeVault depositors
harm.loses_what: ability to withdraw (liveness) until the owner adds ticks
harm.magnitude: all vault funds frozen for the duration

exploit_trace: 1. Market price moves beyond the last configured tick (no boundary found in the loop).
2. getActiveTickIndex returns ticks.length - 3.
3. Any deposit, withdraw (when isEnabled) or rebalance reverts on ticks[ticks.length].

Deposit, withdraw and rebalance revert until price returns or the owner pushes/shifts ticks. Liveness only, owner-recoverable. PoC recommended.

title: TokenisableRange can be emptied to totalSupply 0 and permanently closes, bricking GeVault deposits that include it
description: Discovery: Q5.2 (last call draining everything). deposit() requires totalSupply() > 0 ('TR Closed') but withdraw() has no minimum-liquidity or last-holder protection. GeVault.removeFromAllTicks withdraws its entire TR position on every rebalance/deposit/withdraw. If the vault is the only remaining holder of a TR in its tick list (the 1e18 minted at init may already have been redeemed by the owner), the vault's withdrawal burns the last supply and the next depositAndStash into that tick reverts with 'TR Closed', DoSing deposit, withdraw and rebalance until the owner replaces the tick with modifyTick.
root_cause: No permanent minimum supply is kept in the TR and the closed-state check is applied to internal callers like GeVault.

harm.who: GeVault depositors
harm.loses_what: liveness of deposit/withdraw/rebalance until owner intervenes
harm.magnitude: all vault funds frozen for the duration

exploit_trace: 1. Other holders redeem their TR (including the initial 1e18).
2. GeVault holds 100% of the TR supply; any rebalance calls removeFromTick which burns all of it (totalSupply = 0).
3. deployAssets calls TR.deposit which reverts with 'TR Closed'; vault operations revert.

preconditions.text: GeVault is the sole TR holder of a listed tick

postconditions.text: TR permanently closed

title: RangeManager.removeFromStep (and OPM.withdrawOptionAssets) withdraw TokenisableRange liquidity with amountMin = 0 and no oracle check, unlike OPM.withdrawOptions: LP unwinds are sandwichable
description: Discovery: rescan class 2 (asymmetric operations). OPM.withdrawOptions wraps TokenisableRange.withdraw(amount,0,0) in checkExpectedBalances ('Get output amounts from oracle to avoid sandwich'), and GeVault removes from ticks only behind poolMatchesOracle. RangeManager.removeFromStep calls tokenisedRanges[step].withdraw(trAmt,0,0) and tokenisedTicker[step].withdraw(ttAmt,0,0) with no min amounts, no oracle comparison and no spot guard, and it is reached by removeAssetsFromStep and by every transferAssetsInto*Step call. OPM.withdrawOptionAssets (flashloaned TR in buyOptions) likewise calls TokenisableRange(flashAsset).withdraw(flashAmount,0,0) with no check. TR.withdraw pays out at the Uniswap slot0 composition, so a caller whose pool price was moved in the same block receives an adverse token mix (value at the true price is lower by the position's convexity loss), and the attacker back-runs.
root_cause: TR.withdraw settles at manipulable pool spot composition; the callers that unwind TR positions on a user's behalf in RangeManager and OPM.withdrawOptionAssets pass amount0Min = amount1Min = 0 and perform none of the oracle-value checks used in the sibling paths.
vulnerable_code:
trAmt = LENDING_POOL.withdraw(address(tokenisedRanges[step]), type(uint256).max, address(this));
tokenisedRanges[step].withdraw(trAmt, 0, 0);

harm.who: RangeManager users unwinding or moving ranger/ticker positions (and buyOptions users)
harm.loses_what: part of the position value, realised as the adverse token mix at the manipulated price
harm.magnitude: the LVR/convexity loss of the position for the price displacement the attacker can fund; large for wide rangers, small for 10-tick tickers

exploit_trace: 1. Victim holds aTokens of a wide TokenisableRange (ranger) deposited via RangeManager.
2. Victim submits removeAssetsFromStep(step) (or transferAssetsIntoRangerStep, which calls removeFromStep first).
3. Attacker front-runs by swapping the Uniswap V3 pool so spot moves far inside the ranger's range.

4. removeFromStep PMTransfers the aTokens, withdraws the TR, and tr.withdraw(trAmt,0,0) returns the position's token mix at the manipulated price; cleanup() deposits it to the victim; hf check only looks at debt.
5. Attacker swaps back; the victim is left with tokens worth less than the position at the true price.

TR is a large share of the pool liquidity in its range or the range is wide

postconditions.text: victim's withdrawn tokens are worth less than the position value

title: OPM.executeLiquidation ignores the flashloan premium: the TR re-minted by closeDebt only covers amount plus a tiny dust, so the pool's repayment pull of amount+premium fails
description: Discovery: per-unit step 5 (fee trace) and step 4 (pairing audit: flashloan borrow vs repay). liquidate() flashloans the debt TR with mode 0, so the lending pool pulls back amounts[k] + premiums[k] after executeOperation returns. executeOperation/executeLiquidation never read `premiums`. closeDebt(user == address(this)) mints TR through TokenisableRange.deposit for exactly `amount + addDust()` (dust is about 1e14 TR wei for a 6-decimal asset at $1, see addDust), skips LP.repay, and leaves that TR in the OPM for the pool to pull. With a standard Aave v2 premium (9 bps of amount) the OPM holds amount + ~1e14 TR but must supply amount + 0.0009*amount, so the pull reverts for any non-trivial liquidation unless the ROE pool waives the premium for this receiver (ROE is out of scope and not verified).
root_cause: The repayment side of the flashloan is sized as amount + a fixed dust instead of amount + premium; premiums[] is ignored.

harm.who: liquidators and the protocol (unhealthy positions are not liquidated through OPM)
harm.loses_what: OPM liquidation path is unusable (reverts) when the flashloan premium is non-zero and exceeds dust, leaving bad debt to accumulate
harm.magnitude: liveness of the liquidation feature; premium bps times the liquidated amount is the shortfall

exploit_trace: 1. Position becomes unhealthy; liquidator calls liquidate(poolId, user, [TR], [amount], collateral).
2. LP.flashLoan lends `amount` TR with premium p > 0; executeLiquidation liquidates and closeDebt re-mints about amount + 1e14 TR wei.
3. The pool pulls amount + p TR from the OPM; balance is short by p - 1e14, so the call reverts.

preconditions.text: ROE flashloan premium is non-zero for this receiver and exceeds the dust margin

postconditions.text: OPM liquidations revert

title: closeDebt's self-close 'swap other token back to collateral' runs after every aToken was already PMWithdrawn, so it swaps nothing and the exposure control never happens
description: Discovery: per-unit step 1 (state completeness) and step 2 (branch audit). When user != address(this), closeDebt PMWithdraws the user's entire token0 and token1 aToken balances (amtA, amtB) into the OPM. When user == msg.sender it then calls swapTokens(poolId, otherToken, 0), which reads the user's remaining aToken balance of otherToken (amount==0 branch). That balance is already ~0, so swapTokens returns 0 early (before its cleanup). The leftover underlying stays in the OPM and is simply re-deposited unswapped by close()'s cleanup. The documented intent ('Swap other token back to collateral: this allows to control exposure') is never achieved in the self-close flow.
root_cause: The swap reads the user's aToken balance after it was fully moved into the OPM, instead of swapping the OPM-held leftovers.

harm.who: users who self-close expecting their residual to be converted to collateralAsset
harm.loses_what: no loss of funds; residual exposure to the non-collateral token stays, contrary to the documented behaviour
harm.magnitude: the post-close leftover of the non-collateral token

2. closeDebt PMWithdraws all token0 and token1 aTokens; after repay, leftover token1 sits in the OPM.
3. swapTokens(poolId, token1, 0) sees user's token1 aToken balance == 0 and returns; close() cleanup re-deposits the unswapped token1.

title: GeVault.withdraw pays the whole oracle-valued amount in one chosen token with no swap, so a holder of more than the vault's balance of that token cannot exit and the last holder can never fully withdraw
description: Discovery: per-unit step 3 (boundary values: liquidity = full balance) and step 5 (fee and reward trace). withdraw() computes amount = share of TVL (valueX8) converted to a single caller-chosen token at the oracle price, then calls removeFromAllTicks() and transfers fee and amount - fee of that token. Ticks are single-sided and deployAssets splits holdings across both tokens (ticks[tick0Index..+1] hold token0, ticks[tick1Index..+1] hold token1), so after removal the vault holds both token0 and token1. Nothing converts one into the other. If the share value in the chosen token exceeds the vault's balance of it, safeTransfer reverts. A holder whose share exceeds the vault's holding of either token (any holder near 100% when both sides are non-empty, including the last depositor) cannot withdraw by calling withdraw(0, token) for either token. Only a partial withdrawal bounded by the vault's balance of one token succeeds, after which deployAssets redeploys the remainder 50/50 into both sides again, so each exit round is bounded and pays the treasury fee again.
root_cause: The payout token is chosen by the caller and valued at oracle price, but the vault never rebalances its token mix to the requested token and has no proportional (both-token) payout path.

harm.who: large holders and the last remaining depositor of a GeVault
harm.loses_what: ability to exit in a single transaction; repeated partial exits pay the withdrawal fee on each round and are exposed to price and fee drift between rounds
harm.magnitude: full exit blocked whenever the vault holds both tokens; extra fee of about 0.1-0.3 percent per partial round

exploit_trace: 1. Vault holds TVL V as token0 (about V/2 in value) and token1 (about V/2), deployed in ticks on each side of the price; a single user owns 100 percent of the shares.
2. The user calls withdraw(0, token0): amount = V worth of token0; removeFromAllTicks() returns only about V/2 worth of token0.
3. safeTransfer(treasury, fee) or safeTransfer(msg.sender, bal) reverts on insufficient balance; the same happens for token1.
4. The only way out is multiple partial withdrawals, each capped by the vault's balance of one token, each paying the fee again.

preconditions.text: vault holds both token0 and token1 (the normal deployed state)
the withdrawer's share value in the chosen token exceeds the vault's balance of that token

postconditions.text: withdrawal reverts or is forced into multiple fee-paying partial rounds

title: TokenisableRange.deposit routes the depositor's whole one-sided/off-ratio token amount into the shared fee pool when the position holds none (or little) of that token
description: Discovery: per-unit step 3 (boundary values) and step 1 (state completeness). The fee-pool split computes newFee0 = n0*fee0/(token0Amount+fee0) on the caller's full n0 (and likewise for token1), before Uniswap decides how much of n0 can actually be added. When the position is out of range on the side where token0Amount == 0 and fee0 > 0, newFee0 = n0 and the entire n0 is moved into fee0 (n0 becomes 0). Uniswap would have refunded that token (added0 = 0), but here it is donated pro rata to all LP holders and the depositor receives LP only for the other side. In-range, the same formula charges the fee share on the portion of n0 that will later be refunded, so off-ratio depositors overpay the fee pool by about excess*fee0/(token0Amount+fee0). This is a different root cause from the spot-price manipulation already recorded at TokenisableRange.sol:237.
root_cause: The fee-pool share is taken from the requested n0/n1 rather than from the amounts Uniswap will actually add, and token0Amount == 0 gives a 100% rate.

harm.who: depositors passing both tokens into a TR whose current price is outside its range
harm.loses_what: the token that cannot be added, which should have been refunded, is given to existing LP holders
harm.magnitude: up to the full n0 (or n1) of the deposit when the position holds none of that token and fee > 0; otherwise a small fraction of the unused excess

exploit_trace: 1. TR has fee0 > 0 pending and spot price lies beyond the range so getAmountsForLiquidity returns token0Amount = 0.
2. A user calls deposit(n0, n1) with both n0 > 0 and n1 > 0 (UI/aggregator sends both tokens).
3. newFee0 = n0*fee0/(0+fee0) = n0, so fee0 += n0 and n0 = 0; only n1 is added to Uniswap.
4. The user receives LP only for the n1 liquidity; n0 now belongs pro rata to all LP holders.

preconditions.text: position out of range on one side with fee > 0 on that token, and the caller supplies both tokens

postconditions.text: fee0 or fee1 inflated by the depositor's unused tokens

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓

title: V3Proxy ETH-out paths ignore the result of the final ETH send, so a failed send leaves the user's proceeds stuck in the proxy
description: Discovery: per-unit step 2 (conditional branch audit) and step 5 (asset trace). swapTokensForExactETH, swapExactTokensForETH and swapETHForExactTokens pull the user's input first and then pay out with a low-level call whose success flag is discarded. If msg.sender cannot receive ETH (a contract without a payable receive, or one that reverts), the call fails silently, the transaction succeeds, the Swap event is emitted and the ETH stays in the proxy. emergencyWithdraw only moves ERC20 balances and there is no ETH rescue, so the ETH is unrecoverable. Related: the three ETH-out token functions are marked payable, so ETH sent with them is also never refunded.
root_cause: The success flag of msg.sender.call{value: ...}("") is not checked, and the proxy has no ETH rescue path.
vulnerable_code:
payable(msg.sender).call{value: amounts[1]}("");
emit Swap(msg.sender, path[0], path[1], amounts[0], amounts[1]);

harm.who: contract callers (for example integrators or OPM-like wrappers) that cannot accept ETH
harm.loses_what: the full ETH output of the swap, or the unspent ETH refund
harm.magnitude: up to the swap output or refund amount per call

exploit_trace: 1. A contract without a payable receive calls swapExactTokensForETH(amountIn, ...).
2. The router returns WETH to the proxy, the proxy unwraps it, and the call to msg.sender fails with the result ignored.
3. Result: the transaction succeeds, the user's tokens are spent, and the ETH stays in the proxy with no function able to return it.

preconditions.text: the caller is a contract that rejects plain ETH transfers

postconditions.text: ETH is locked in V3Proxy

title: RangeManager.removeFromStep reverts for the whole step if either the range or the ticker reserve is not listed in the lending pool
description: Discovery: per-unit step 2 (conditional branch audit). removeFromStep unconditionally calls ERC20(LENDING_POOL.getReserveData(tokenisedRanges[step]).aTokenAddress).balanceOf(msg.sender) and the same for tokenisedTicker[step]. generateRange creates both tokens, but listing them as reserves is a separate lending-pool admin action. For an unlisted token aTokenAddress is address(0), so the balanceOf call to a non-contract reverts. removeAssetsFromStep and both transferAssetsInto*Step functions, which all go through removeFromStep, then revert for that step even if the user only holds the other (listed) token.
root_cause: The ticker/range legs are not guarded against a zero aTokenAddress, and removeFromStep handles both legs in one call.
vulnerable_code: trAmt = ERC20(LENDING_POOL.getReserveData(address(tokenisedTicker[step])).aTokenAddress).balanceOf(msg.sender);

harm.loses_what: ability to exit or rebalance through RangeManager until the other reserve is listed
harm.magnitude: temporary DoS; funds recoverable by withdrawing directly from the lending pool

exploit_trace: 1. Owner calls generateRange; only the Range token is listed as a ROE reserve.
2. A user deposits the Range token and later calls removeAssetsFromStep(step).
3. The ticker's getReserveData returns aTokenAddress 0 and balanceOf reverts, so the whole call reverts.

preconditions.text: one of the step's two tokens is not a lending pool reserve

postconditions.text: RangeManager entry points for that step are unusable

title: LPOracle.latestAnswer multiplies a*b*priceA unscaled in uint256 and reverts for large pools
description: Discovery: per-unit step 3 (boundary values). a and b are uint112 reserves, so a*b can reach 2^224; multiplying by an 8-decimal price (and 10**(decB-decA)) before the sqrt overflows 2^256 for pools with large raw reserves (high-supply or high-decimals tokens). The code comment acknowledges the overflow but the mitigation only covers the decimals ratio.
root_cause: a * b * priceA is computed in full before division and sqrt; checked arithmetic reverts on overflow.
vulnerable_code: norm_b = sqrt( a * b * priceA * 10**(decimalsB-decimalsA) / priceB );

harm.who: lending market consuming the LP oracle
harm.loses_what: price availability: borrows, withdrawals and liquidations of LP collateral revert
harm.magnitude: all positions collateralised by the affected LP

exploit_trace: 1. LP pool reserves a,b grow so a*b*priceA > 2^256 (e.g. a*b ~ 1e66 raw units).
2. latestAnswer() reverts with Panic(0x11).
3. Result: oracle consumers cannot price the LP token.

preconditions.text: pair reserves large enough that a*b*priceA exceeds 2^256

postconditions.text: oracle reverts for the LP token

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✗ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
postconditions_created: oracle reverts for the LP token

verdict.reason: LPOracle is the known Alpha Finance/Inverse fair-LP-price design; the overflow is acknowledged in the code comment and only occurs for pools with extreme raw reserves not in scope.

title: OracleConvert.latestRoundData reports block.timestamp and max round ids, hiding stale or non-positive component feeds
description: Discovery: per-unit step 3 and 2. getAnswer only checks updatedAt > 0 and does not check price > 0 or freshness. latestAnswer casts int to uint (negative becomes huge, causing revert or absurd product; zero yields price 0). latestRoundData then returns updatedAt = block.timestamp and answeredInRound = type(uint80).max, so any consumer doing a standard staleness / round-completeness check on this oracle always passes even if the underlying feeds are stale.
root_cause: Composite round data is synthesised from the current block instead of from the component feeds' updatedAt/round data; component price sign/zero not validated.
vulnerable_code: uint priceA = uint(getAnswer(CL_TOKENA)); ... return (type(uint80).max, latestAnswer(), block.timestamp, block.timestamp, type(uint80).max);

harm.who: protocols consuming OracleConvert via latestRoundData
harm.loses_what: staleness protection; collateral/debt valued at stale or zero prices
harm.magnitude: depends on feed staleness

exploit_trace: 1. One component Chainlink feed stops updating (or returns 0).
2. Consumer calls latestRoundData(); updatedAt == block.timestamp so freshness check passes.
3. Result: stale or zero composite price is accepted.

preconditions.text: a component feed is stale or returns <=0 and consumer relies on latestRoundData freshness

postconditions.text: stale/zero price accepted as fresh

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✗
depth_evidence: [TRACE:feed stale → latestAnswer uses old price → latestRoundData updatedAt=now]
postconditions_created: stale/zero price accepted as fresh

verdict.reason: README known issue: oracle liveness/staleness is not checked in the contracts (Aave pool fails on stale/zero feeds).

title: GeVault.deposit mints shares against a TVL that excludes idle funds, so after a disabled-pool withdrawal the next deposit is priced at a fixed $1/share and then absorbs all idle funds
description:
Coupled Pair: totalSupply() (GEV shares) <-> vault asset value (token0/token1 balances held idle + aTokens of TRs)
Breaking Operation: withdraw() with isEnabled == false (removeFromAllTicks, no deployAssets), then deposit() after setEnabled(true)
Masking Code: deposit() branch `if (tSupply == 0 || vaultValueX8 == 0) liquidity = valueX8 * 1e10` treats TVL == 0 as an empty vault regardless of tSupply
Cross-Feed: DB-1, DB-2
getTVL() sums only TR aToken balances; it ignores token0/token1 sitting in the vault. While the pool is disabled, withdraw() pulls every TR out of the lending pool and Uniswap and leaves the remainder idle, so getTVL() == 0 while totalSupply() > 0. When the owner re-enables the pool, the first deposit() sees vaultValueX8 == 0 and mints valueX8 * 1e10 shares at a fixed $1 per 1e18 shares, ignoring existing supply, and the following rebalance() deploys all idle funds, which now count as backing the new shares as well.
root_cause: Invariant: share price = (all assets owned by the vault) / totalSupply. getTVL() omits idle token balances, and deposit() special-cases TVL == 0 without checking totalSupply, so the minted share count is unrelated to the real price of existing shares whenever funds are idle.

harm.who: existing GEV holders (or the new depositor, depending on whether the real share price is above or below $1)
harm.loses_what: share of the idle assets, repriced by the ratio of the real share price to the fixed $1 mint price
harm.magnitude: proportional to the deviation of the real share price from $1 times the idle value; bounded by idle vault assets

exploit_trace: 1. Owner calls setEnabled(false); a holder calls withdraw(); removeFromAllTicks() moves all TR liquidity to idle token0/token1 and deployAssets() is skipped.
2. The remaining holders' value sits idle in the vault; getTVL() returns 0 while totalSupply() > 0.
3. Owner calls setEnabled(true) to resume operations.
4. Attacker deposit()s a small amount when the real share price is above $1 (fees accrued): vaultValueX8 == 0 so liquidity = valueX8 * 1e10, i.e. $1 per share.
5. rebalance() deploys all idle funds; the attacker's shares now represent a larger fraction of the full vault than the amount paid, and redeems at the real price for profit.

preconditions.text: owner disables the pool and funds remain idle after a withdrawal, then re-enables
real share price differs from $1

postconditions.text: share supply mispriced relative to the vault's assets

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✓ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R8:✓(TVL read in deposit and withdraw)
postconditions_created: share price reset to $1 anchor
audit_trail.who_benefits: Depositor arriving after pool re-enable when the real share price exceeds $1

verdict.reason: Coupled-state inconsistency confirmed (GeVault.sol:274-275 treats vaultValueX8==0 as an empty vault regardless of supply; getTVL ignores idle funds). Needs the owner to disable then re-enable the pool after a withdrawal and a real share price different from $1; profit bounded by (p-1) times a deposit capped by tvlCap. Downgraded from Medium; extends DB-1.

title: GeVault.modifyTick overwrites a ticks[] entry without unwinding the vault's position in the replaced TokenisableRange, orphaning those funds and collapsing the share price
description:
Coupled Pair: ticks[] (addresses of TRs tracked by the vault) <-> aToken balances of TRs actually held by the vault in the lending pool
Breaking Operation: modifyTick()
Cross-Feed: DP3-2
getTVL(), getReserves(), removeFromAllTicks() and withdraw() iterate only over ticks[]. modifyTick() replaces ticks[index] with a new TR without first calling removeFromTick(index), so any aTokens the vault holds for the old TR are no longer counted or withdrawable. TVL drops by that value, and new deposits are minted against the understated TVL, diluting existing holders; the stranded position can only be recovered by re-adding the old TR address.
root_cause: Invariant: every TR for which the vault holds aTokens is in ticks[]. modifyTick() (an owner-only mutation, also shiftTick/pushTick never remove) breaks it by dropping the old entry while a balance may exist.
vulnerable_code:
ticks[index] = TokenisableRange(tr);
emit ModifyTick(tr, index);

harm.who: GEV holders
harm.loses_what: value of the orphaned TR position (until the owner restores it), plus dilution through deposits minted against an understated TVL
harm.magnitude: value of the replaced tick's position, potentially a large share of TVL

exploit_trace: 1. Vault has deployed funds; ticks[k] = TR_A and the vault holds aTR_A.
2. Owner calls modifyTick(TR_B, k) without calling rebalance/removing first (or a deposit lands in between).
3. getTVL() no longer includes aTR_A; withdraw() and rebalance() never remove it.
4. A depositor mints shares against the understated TVL and later redeems after the owner restores TR_A, capturing the orphaned value.

preconditions.text: owner calls modifyTick on an index with a non-zero vault position

postconditions.text: vault TVL understated; funds stranded in lending pool

audit_trail.step_execution: Gates: A=✓ B=✓ C=✓ D=✓ E=✗ F=✓ G=✓ H=✓
rules_applied: R12:✓(enumerated writers of ticks: pushTick, shiftTick, modifyTick)
postconditions_created: orphaned aToken position
audit_trail.who_benefits: Depositor entering during the understated-TVL window

verdict.reason: Owner-only modifyTick called without first unwinding the old tick: admin error, no unprivileged trigger.
